page: Google Cloud Platform c4-highmem-16 is a memory-optimized virtual machine instance configured with 16 dedicated vCPUs and 124 GB of RAM. Powered by an Intel Xeon 8581C processor operating at 2.3 GHz, the instance features 8 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled. The underlying x86_64 architecture includes a 260 MB L3 cache, 2 MB L2 cache, and 48 KB L1d cache. It does not include local NVMe SSD storage or bundled GPUs, relying entirely on network-attached storage for persistent disk operations.

Benchmark evaluations demonstrate strong single-core performance, with Geekbench single-core and text processing scores reaching top-tier levels in the top 10% category. Single-threaded gzip compression and bzip3 decompression also show strong performance in the top 25% tier. Multi-core operations, such as stress-ng multi-core CPU performance and Geekbench multi-core scores, align with average tier expectations. The instance lacks local storage and GPU accelerators, which limits its suitability for workloads requiring high-speed local IOPS or hardware-accelerated graphics processing.

From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the c4-highmem-16 provides a high memory-to-vCPU ratio of 7.75 GB per core, making it a resource-dense option for memory-bound workloads without the overhead of excess compute cores. It is well-suited for database operations, software compilation, text processing, and moderate-scale LLM inference tasks, such as prompt processing and text generation using small to medium models.
